correctness.rationale: In the exact inclusion–exclusion numerator 15!D the odd-j coefficients are positive and the even-j coefficients negative. The factorial has valuation 11. For the odd bases x_j=j^(2^n)-1 has valuation at least n+2, and q_j=x_j/2^n obeys q_(j,n+1)=q_(j,n)+2^(n-1)q_(j,n)^2; the increment is a multiple of 8192 for n>=10. Direct powers give the listed eight residues and their weighted sum 4096 mod 8192, so the linear odd moment has valuation n+12. For d=a-b, Vandermonde and h*binom(d,h)=d*binom(d-1,h-1) show that the binomial-coefficient difference at order t has valuation at least r-floor(log2 t) whenever nonzero. For t>=2 the bound t(n+2)-floor(log2 t)>=2n+3>=n+13 forces every higher term above the linear term, hence the odd numerator has valuation n+r+12. Among even j, bases with just one factor of two give their binomial coefficients modulo 128 after division by 2^(b*2^n), because odd units raised to 2^n are 1 mod 128 and j^(d*2^n) vanishes mod 128. Higher-valuation bases do not contribute modulo 128. The coefficient sum 8128 gives valuation b*2^n+6 in the even numerator. Unequal valuations give the lower one; equality gives at least one more factor of two and no exact boundary value is asserted. T increases without bound for fixed b, giving the eventual fixed-pair formula. Independent replay: python3 -B /workspace/reproduce_frozen.py 5 evaluates the base powers with integer arithmetic, checks the even sum, probes both strict regimes and resonance, and checks small pairs by the Stirling recurrence. An infinite displayed diagnostic means zero at the test precision, not an infinite valuation of D.
